claim: For every K4-free graph the triangle cover number (least number of triangle-free subgraphs covering the edges) is at most the triangle-free chromatic ceiling (the supremum of chromatic numbers of triangle-free subgraphs); and more generally, for any linear order on the vertices, the triangle cover number is at most the supremum over vertices of the chromatic number of the subgraph induced on the neighbours lying above that vertex, which yields that every graph on kappa-plus vertices is a union of kappa triangle-free subgraphs.

facets.entities: K4-free graphs, their triangle-free edge decompositions, neighbourhood subgraphs, linear orders on the vertex set
facets.mechanism: colour each edge by the colour that the smaller endpoint's neighbourhood colouring assigns to the larger endpoint, so the two edges at the least vertex of any triangle differ
facets.method: well-ordering the vertex set, degeneracy and colouring number arguments, neighbourhood chromatic bounds
facets.outcome: an upper bound on the triangle cover number by a chromatic invariant, and the corollary that no graph on aleph-one vertices needs uncountably many triangle-free layers
